glass: tall highball glass (about 300 ml), chilled in the freezer, 1-inch ice cubes added one at a time
version: v1 (round 2, 2026-10-02): a Whisky Highball built the Codex's careful way (EXPLORING TECHNIQUE: BUILDING WHISKY HIGHBALLS, p. 214: two parts cold seltzer to one of whisky, chilled glass, 1-inch cubes lowered one at a time, stir until the glass mists, lift the bottom cube an inch to mix, one final turn). Core: an unpeated Highland single malt from bourbon casks, no sherry or wine finish, as a style (no named bottle; 40% typical, swept 40-46%). Spark: 1/8 teaspoon pure vanilla extract stirred into the whisky first (Flavor Matrix pdf 256: whiskey is among vanilla's best pairings; Oxford MATURATION pdf 1265 and BOTANICAL pdf 321: vanillin is one of the flavours an oak cask gives a spirit). It names, in the glass, the cask Barnard's record barely mentions; declared in the recipe, never hidden (against Oxford FLAVORED SYRUP pdf 809's synthetic vanillin used to amplify a whisky). No lemon, no sugar.
